predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: the counties of Anjou and Maine, which King John II gave to his son Louis in 1356 ('His father appointed him count of Anjou and Maine in 1356')

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the duchy of Anjou (reunited to the royal domain on René's death in July 1480) and Provence (bequeathed to Louis XI by Charles III on 10 December 1481)

successors.name: Duchy of Lorraine
successors.text: the duchy of Bar, which René's will of 1474 left to his grandson René II, Duke of Lorraine

rulers.name: Louis I
rulers.title: Count of Anjou and Maine 1356, Duke of Anjou 1360, Count of Provence 1382

rulers.name: René
rulers.title: Duke of Anjou, Count of Provence; Duke of Bar from 1430 and of Lorraine from 1431

rulers.name: Charles IV
rulers.title: Count of Maine, Duke of Anjou and Count of Provence (Charles III of Provence)

ledger.x: 1356: King John II gives Anjou and Maine to his son Louis, founding the house.
25 October 1360: Louis I's county of Anjou is raised by letters patent to 'a duchy in the peerage of France'.
1370: Louis I becomes duke of Touraine ('duke of Anjou in 1360 and duke of Touraine in 1370').
1382: Louis I succeeds Joanna I in Provence.
1382: the Union of Aix forms against Louis I.
1388: Nice and the Terres Neuves de Provence pass under the House of Savoy (the dedition of Nice).

ledger.cp: Duchy of Bar (Louis, Cardinal of Bar)

ledger.x: 1431: René succeeds his father-in-law as Duke of Lorraine, but loses at Bulgneville in July 1431 to Antoine de Vaudemont ('backed by Burgundian forces') and is captured.
1476: Louis XI reconciles with René and restores Anjou to him.
10 July 1480: René dies at Aix and Anjou goes to the crown.
1480: Bar passes to René II of Lorraine.
December 1481: the last Angevin count dies and Provence goes to the crown.

wars.name: Union of Aix revolt in Provence
wars.outcome: The Union of Aix, formed in 1382 by followers of Charles of Naples, opposed Louis of Anjou; Louis held western Provence.

wars.name: Lorraine succession and the Battle of Bulgneville
wars.outcome: René was beaten at Bulgneville in July 1431 and captured; he was released on parole in April 1432 and Emperor Sigismund confirmed him as Duke of Lorraine at Basel in 1434.

wars.name: Angevin claims to the Kingdom of Naples
wars.outcome: Louis I invaded Naples in 1382 and died there in 1384; Louis II was crowned at Avignon in 1389 and lost to Ladislaus in 1399; René was King of Naples from 1435 and was driven out by Alfonso V in 1442.

wars.name: Louis XI's seizure of Anjou and Bar
wars.outcome: Louis XI seized the duchy after René's will of 22 July 1474 and restored it to René in 1476; Anjou went to the crown for good on René's death in 1480.

certainty.note: Apanage and inherited lands: the Duchy page gives Anjou only as 'roughly co-extensive with the diocese of Angers'; Provence's eastern frontier was the Union of Aix front in 1382-1387 and the Savoyard line from 1388.
